protected_assets: nonce uniqueness and replay-safe stored ciphertext
adversaries: same-user process compromise is not contained by H0

trust_boundaries.provider_binary: Exact provider image and dependency closure must be identified; file hash alone is not publisher authenticity.
trust_boundaries.protocol_context: Typed domain, app, space, epoch, object and recipient context remain outside primitive trust and must be verified by PAR code.
trust_boundaries.authorization: Valid signatures and HPKE packages do not imply membership/control authorization.
trust_boundaries.harness: Local receipts are integrity-bound evidence, not an independent security attestation.
trust_boundaries.platform_keystore: Hardware/software protection class must be read back on each supported target and may not silently downgrade.

key_lifecycle.restore_rule: Restored writers use a new actor generation and remain write-disabled until current authority is re-established.
key_lifecycle.export_rule: Data exports do not carry plaintext recovery secrets; secret display/copy is a separate consented operation.
key_lifecycle.rotation_rule: Compromise response must support key replacement and data evacuation without reviving stale authority.

randomness_and_nonce.rng: OS CSPRNG only; RNG failure aborts the write.
randomness_and_nonce.nonce: Persist reservation before encryption when uniqueness is stateful; never reuse an abandoned nonce.
randomness_and_nonce.retry: After commit uncertainty, query by stable operation ID and reuse stored ciphertext rather than re-encrypting.
randomness_and_nonce.test_determinism: Deterministic randomness is allowed only in explicit KAT/test paths.

serialization_and_migration.canonical_context: Existing typed canonical encoding and domain separation remain authoritative.
serialization_and_migration.ciphertext_compatibility: A provider replacement must preserve the frozen PAR suite bytes or ship an explicit versioned migration profile.
serialization_and_migration.no_resign_unknown: Unknown semantic fields or suites are preserved/rejected according to compatibility rules and are never stripped and re-signed.
serialization_and_migration.migration: Dual-read/single-write migration requires exact suite/provider generation metadata and rollback-safe checkpoints before activation.

requirements: reproducible or independently cross-checked build where practical
known-vulnerability and maintenance review at decision time

platform_key_protection.rule: Report the actually verified protection class; hardware-backed claims require target readback/evidence and no silent software fallback.

candidate_families.reason: Minimizes change to existing Ed25519/X25519/XChaCha paths but still needs a maintained provider image, strict-vector review, dependency closure and a separately reviewed HPKE implementation.
Could unify native wrappers and HPKE in the Rust lane, but exact crates, audit history, interoperability and FFI/key-lifecycle costs must be reviewed before selection.
May improve device key protection but cannot be assumed to implement the complete frozen PAR primitive suite consistently across platforms.

required_security_evidence: maintained provider release/source/binary identity and dependency closure
public primitive KATs plus strict malformed/non-canonical/low-order reject corpus
control-chain and real CRDT trust-boundary integration
independent security review before product promotion
stop_conditions: provider choice would change the frozen wire/ciphertext format without an approved migration
provider requires silent algorithm or implementation fallback
dependency closure or maintenance status cannot be established
key-protection class cannot be observed and downgrade would be silent
security qualification relies only on provider self-declaration or local tests
legacy libsodium 1.0.18 would be promoted beyond disposable experiment scope
